Subject: RE: Clarify SOW acceptance criteria + pricing-floor redlines (Order Form #4721)

Team —

Read AcuHealth's redlines. Quick legal read and proposed approach below (I attached a clean markup).

Acceptance testing (Exhibit A)
- Risk: their requested automatic credits after a 14-day remediation is aggressive. It creates open-ended exposure if integration requires deeper fixes.
- Proposal: preserve our standard 21-calendar-day acceptance window, but add clearer pass/fail criteria in Exhibit A (sample test cases, success thresholds, and a remediation plan). If remediation extends beyond 21 days, customer is eligible for a limited, capped service credit (e.g., up to 10% of the monthly recurring charge prorated for the impacted month).

Pricing floor / burst caps
- Risk: a guaranteed maximum effective per-GPU rate (your discounts capped) materially limits our pricing levers and could reduce flexibility to manage cluster utilization.
- Proposal: Add a "rate-guard" clause that: (a) guarantees a capped per-GPU effective rate for burst usage up to X hours/month (we recommend X = 300 hours), and (b) allows us to apply higher on-demand rates beyond that cap. Alternatively, we can offer a tiered cap tied to a nominal premium for guaranteed burst pricing.

Billing cadence
- Net-30 is OK; we should insist on line-item consumption detail for burst usage as part of the acceptance deliverables.

Next steps
1) Naomi / Commercial to confirm whether we are comfortable with the 300-hour guard or prefer a different threshold.
2) I will circulate a redline (redwood_legal_response_v1.pdf) with the alternative language for AcuHealth to review.
3) If AcuHealth accepts the capped credit approach and the rate-guard threshold, Legal is comfortable moving forward.

Ben
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_legal_response_v1.pdf (PDF)]

Subject: RE: Clarify SOW acceptance criteria + pricing-floor redlines (Order Form #4721)

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the redlines and for agreeing to a quick sync. We discussed internally and here's a consolidated position:

- Acceptance testing: Redwood will accept explicit acceptance criteria in Exhibit A. We propose 21 calendar days for the acceptance/remediation window, with a capped service credit formula if remediation extends beyond that period (credit capped at 10% of monthly recurring charges for the impacted month). This keeps a clear remediation path while limiting open-ended financial exposure.

- Pricing floor / burst: We can offer a rate-guard for burst capacity capped at 300 GPU-hours/month at an effective per-GPU-hour ceiling of $4.50; usage beyond that will be billed at on-demand rates per the Order Form. If AcuHealth prefers a different cap, we can negotiate a tiered premium.

- Billing cadence: Net-30 acceptable. We will provide line-item breakdowns for burst usage in the monthly invoice.

I've uploaded a consolidated SOW/Order Form draft with our suggested language to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFgHIjK-acuhealth-orderform (see "sow_acceptance_draft.docx" and "redwood_legal_response_v1.pdf").

Can you confirm by EOD if AcuHealth can accept the 21-day window and the 300-hour rate-guard at $4.50/hr? If yes, we'll prep a final order form and route for DocuSign. If you want a brief call to finalize wording, Ben and Karthik are available 2–3pm PT today.

Best,
Naomi
